voice: male, English, for Indian and global viewers aged 18-35; say 'Sivakasi' slowly (SHIV-uh-KAH-see); explain Deepavali, crore and lakh once
status: DRAFT v1 for AK review, 1 Nov 2026. NOT CLEARED FOR VOICING: every claim is BRIEF-ONLY or QUARANTINED. Not voiced.
format: F1 Myth Flip, told on a planet → region → place → people → planet ladder; general audience, no channel branding

beats.say: Every Deepavali, India's festival of lights, the sky fills with fireworks. By the industry's own count, between eighty and ninety percent of them are made in and around one town. Sivakasi.
beats.caption: 80-90% · one town
beats.visual: Night sky over India fades to a map; a single pin drops on south Tamil Nadu

beats.say: You'd guess a craft like that is ancient. Passed down for centuries, from father to son.
beats.caption: Ancient tradition?
beats.visual: Old-style woodcut hands rolling paper tubes (tagged artistic); a question mark

beats.say: It isn't. A hundred years ago, Sivakasi made no fireworks at all. It didn't even make matches.
beats.caption: Before 1923: none
beats.visual: The drawn hands fade out; a blank map of the town

beats.say: So how does a town that made nothing end up lighting India's sky? The answer starts with a matchbox, a long train ride, and two young men.
beats.caption: HOW?
beats.visual: Matchbox slides in; rail line draws south to north-east

beats.say: Follow the chain. Each link lights the next.
beats.caption: THE CHAIN
beats.visual: Four small icons in a row, dark: match, coloured flame, printing press, firework

beats.say: Find India on the globe. Now slide down to its far south, to Tamil Nadu.
beats.caption: Tamil Nadu
beats.visual: Globe spin, zoom to the southern state

beats.say: Sivakasi sits in Virudhunagar district. It is hot, and it sits in the rain shadow of the hills to the west.
beats.caption: Virudhunagar district
beats.visual: Terrain map; rain arrows stop at the ridge (geodata for the ridge, artistic arrows tagged)

beats.say: Farming here has always been hard. The soil is dry and the rain is short. Remember that dryness. It comes back.
beats.caption: Dry. Remember it.
beats.visual: Cracked black soil
beats.optional: Cut with f09o if C031 has no source

beats.say: Three things to keep in mind. A match. A Bengal light, which is a match that burns in colour. And a firework.
beats.caption: Match · Bengal light · Firework
beats.visual: Three icons labelled one by one

beats.say: Go back to nineteen twenty-two. Matches are made in Calcutta, today's Kolkata, or shipped in from abroad.
beats.caption: 1922 · Calcutta
beats.visual: Old-map style India; Calcutta glows

beats.say: It is a very long way north-east of Sivakasi. A long train ride.
beats.caption: Sivakasi → Kolkata
beats.visual: Ruler line draws between the two points with a km counter (value inserted after C032 is measured)
beats.note: Insert the measured straight-line km only after C032 is computed from a sourced Sivakasi point. Do not use the bible's '2,000 km'.

beats.say: Two young men from Sivakasi make that trip. P. Ayya Nadar is about seventeen. A. Shanmuga Nadar is about nineteen.
beats.caption: Ayya Nadar · Shanmuga Nadar
beats.visual: Two drawn silhouettes at a station (no archival portraits unless the licence is cleared)

beats.say: They aren't going to learn fireworks. They're going to learn one thing: how to make a safety match.
beats.caption: Goal: the safety match
beats.visual: Close-up of a drawn matchbox

beats.say: They stay six to eight months, learning from a match-maker named Purna Chandra Roy.
beats.caption: 6-8 months
beats.visual: Workshop scene, slow

beats.say: In nineteen twenty-three they come home with German machines and open a match factory. The South-India Lucifer Match Industry.
beats.caption: 1923 · first match factory
beats.visual: Machines arrive by cart; factory sign draws in

beats.say: So far: matches. Not one firework. Where do the fireworks come from? Keep watching.
beats.caption: Matches. Not fireworks.
beats.visual: Matchbox centre; empty slot where a firework would be

beats.say: But the heavy German machines are a problem. In a small, remote town, they are costly to run.
beats.caption: Machines: too costly
beats.visual: Machine stamped with a cost tag

beats.say: So the founders change the plan. They spread the work across the villages around.
beats.caption: Spread the work
beats.visual: Map: lines from the factory to nearby villages

beats.say: It fits the mood of the time. Mahatma Gandhi is urging Indians to revive village industries.
beats.caption: Village industry
beats.visual: Gandhi-era poster style, drawn in code (artistic)

beats.say: Families roll, fill and pack by hand, at home. The factory does only the chemical part.
beats.caption: Hands at home
beats.visual: Drawn verandah scene, women and children packing

beats.say: Think of many home kitchens feeding one restaurant, instead of one giant kitchen. Cheap to start. Hard to supervise.
beats.caption: Many kitchens, one brand
beats.visual: Verandahs link to one factory by lines

beats.say: Remember that choice. It builds the town. And a hundred years later, it is the hardest thing to change.
beats.caption: Remember: hands
beats.visual: Hold on the verandah scene

beats.say: In nineteen twenty-six the two men part ways, and compete. Ayya Nadar's brand is a squirrel, Anil. Shanmuga Nadar's is a crow, Kaaka. A squirrel against a crow.
beats.caption: Squirrel vs Crow
beats.visual: Two label designs drawn in code, side by side

beats.say: To stand out, match-makers add something new: sticks that burn in colour. They're called Bengal lights. In Tamil, matthaappu.
beats.caption: Bengal light · matthaappu
beats.visual: A match strikes; the flame turns red, then green

beats.say: Local histories treat the Bengal light as the stepping stone. A match that burns in colour is already close to a sparkler. And in nineteen thirty-eight, N. R. K. Rajarathina Nadar opens the town's first factory made only for fireworks.
beats.caption: 1938 · first fireworks factory
beats.visual: Match flame grows into a sparkler, then a first firework
beats.hedge: 'treat ... as' is the hedge until C014 has a source

beats.say: That answers our first question. Matches led to coloured matches. Coloured matches led to fireworks. Not a tradition. A chain.
beats.caption: Not a tradition. A chain.
beats.visual: First two icons of the chain light up

beats.say: Every matchbox and every packet of crackers needs a bright paper label. In the nineteen thirties, those labels come from presses in Bombay, today's Mumbai.
beats.caption: Labels from Bombay
beats.visual: Label rolls on a train, Mumbai to Sivakasi

beats.say: So in nineteen thirty-eight, K. S. A. Arunagiri Nadar sets up a printing press in Sivakasi itself. National Litho Press.
beats.caption: 1938 · National Litho Press
beats.visual: Press frame draws in

beats.say: Picture a shop that sells most of its stock in one week, and keeps running out of paper cups from a far-off city. So the owner buys a printer. Then he notices it can print for the other eleven months too.
beats.caption: One week. Eleven months.
beats.visual: Drawn shop; calendar flips

beats.say: That is Sivakasi's second trick. When the fireworks season ends, the presses keep running. Calendars. Diaries. Notebooks.
beats.caption: Presses never stop
beats.visual: Press output: calendar, diary, notebook
beats.note: C021 is unsourced: keep the sentence general, no month ranges

beats.say: Prime Minister Nehru is said to have called the town 'Kutty Japan', Little Japan, for making matches, fireworks and print on its own.
beats.caption: 'Kutty Japan'
beats.visual: Nameplate

beats.say: A historian of the town, Rengaiah Murugan, put it simply: 'As a chain reaction, various allied industries started to mushroom.'
beats.caption: Chain reaction
beats.visual: Quote card over the chain icons

beats.say: So three links so far. The match. The coloured flame. The press. One more is coming, and it is not a machine. It is a war.
beats.caption: Match · colour · press · ?
beats.visual: Chain: three lit, one dark

beats.say: Now comes the moment that turns a good town into the national one. Nineteen-forty.
beats.visual: Black beat, then a date

beats.say: That year, the Explosives Rules arrive. To make fireworks, you now need a licence.
beats.caption: Licence required
beats.visual: Rule document draws in

beats.say: Then the Second World War cuts off the fireworks that used to come in from abroad.
beats.caption: Imports stop
beats.visual: Sea routes close on the map

beats.say: The few licensed makers suddenly have the whole market. By nineteen forty-two, three firms hold licences: National, Standard and Kaliswari.
beats.caption: National · Standard · Kaliswari
beats.visual: Three factory icons

beats.say: Three licensed factories in nineteen forty-two.
beats.visual: Bar chart: one bar rises

beats.say: By nineteen eighty: a hundred and eighty-nine.
beats.visual: Bar rises

beats.say: By two thousand and one: four hundred and fifty.
beats.visual: Bar rises

beats.say: Today, the industry says, more than a thousand.
beats.caption: Today: 1,000+
beats.visual: Bar rises past the frame

beats.say: Worth about six thousand crore rupees a year. That is sixty billion rupees.
beats.caption: ₹6,000 crore a year
beats.visual: Counter ticks to 6,000 as the whole chain glows

beats.move: Payoff of the plant (cut if C031 fails)
beats.say: And the makers say one more thing helps: the sun. Paper tubes and chemicals must dry in the open. Dry, sunny Sivakasi dries them for free.
beats.caption: Dry sun = free drying
beats.visual: Drying yard, time-lapse shadows
beats.optional: Cut with b03o if C031 has no source

beats.say: So here is the real story, in one line. Sivakasi didn't inherit fireworks. It copied a matchbox, coloured the flame, printed its own labels, and a war closed the door behind it.
beats.caption: COPY · COLOUR · PRINT · WAR
beats.visual: All four chain icons light in order

beats.say: Today's challenge comes from a new direction. The air.
beats.caption: The air
beats.visual: Delhi winter haze (drawn)

beats.say: In October twenty-eighteen, the Supreme Court bans crackers made with barium salts, and joined crackers. The aim is cleaner air in the north.
beats.caption: Oct 2018 · ban
beats.visual: Court order frame

beats.say: The industry's answer is the green cracker, developed by a government lab, CSIR-NEERI. Its versions are called SWAS, SAFAL and STAR.
beats.caption: Green crackers
beats.visual: Three labels

beats.say: Green doesn't mean pollution-free. The lab's own claim is about a third less particle pollution.
beats.caption: ~30% less. Not zero.
beats.visual: Smoke density bars: before, after

beats.say: How? According to the lab, the mix releases water vapour and air as it burns, which helps the dust settle. Picture a tiny mist sprayer inside the shell.
beats.caption: Water vapour settles dust
beats.visual: Cutaway of a drawn shell with mist

beats.say: Delhi and its surroundings are roughly thirteen percent of national demand, industry associations estimate.
beats.caption: Delhi-NCR ≈ 13%
beats.visual: Map highlight

beats.say: In October twenty twenty-five, the Court eases the Delhi ban: green crackers only, with QR codes, in fixed time slots. But it comes just before Deepavali. A makers' leader said it comes too close to the festival, yet gives hope for future business.
beats.caption: Oct 2025 · too close to the festival
beats.visual: Calendar countdown to Deepavali

beats.say: So the law gave a ban, then a lab, then a compromise. And a deadline that arrived too late for this season.
beats.caption: Ban · lab · compromise
beats.visual: Three steps lit

beats.say: Now go back to the hands. By the industry's count, about three lakh people work in these factories. That is three hundred thousand. Many more work around them.
beats.caption: ~3 lakh workers
beats.visual: Drawn crowd leaving a factory gate

beats.say: Mixing, filling and threading fuses are still done mostly by hand.
beats.caption: Still by hand
beats.visual: Hands, close
beats.note: C029 quarantined: needs a source before this beat can be voiced

beats.say: On paper, a small unit's licence limits how many people may work inside. Reports say twelve.
beats.caption: Licence cap
beats.visual: Floor plan
beats.optional: Cut unless C027 gets a source

beats.say: Reports describe sheds sub-let to contractors, and crowded verandahs. A gap between the licence and the workplace.
beats.caption: Licence ≠ workplace
beats.visual: Floor plan with more figures than the cap

beats.say: On the nineteenth of April, twenty twenty-six, an explosion at a factory near Sivakasi killed twenty-five workers.
beats.caption: 19 Apr 2026 · 25 killed
beats.visual: Sober frame: date, number, a lamp. No gore, no photos

beats.say: A worker, K. Rajkumar, told The Hindu that with a biometric attendance system, identifying the dead would not have been so hard.
beats.caption: Who was inside?
beats.visual: Attendance ledger frame

beats.say: The choice the founders made in nineteen twenty-three, spread the work across many hands, built the town. Now the same choice needs a new safety answer.
beats.caption: The same hands
beats.visual: Verandah scene from d03, now with the floor-plan overlay

beats.say: In May twenty twenty-five, the makers' association applied for a GI tag for Sivakasi fireworks. It's a legal label of origin. Their lawyer says it would help curb duplicates.
beats.caption: GI tag applied · May 2025
beats.visual: GI application frame

beats.say: A matchbox. A coloured flame. A printing press. A war. A hundred years.
beats.caption: Match · colour · press · war
beats.visual: Chain icons, all lit

beats.say: So that Deepavali sky wasn't made by an ancient tradition. It was made by a town that kept learning.
beats.caption: Not tradition. Learning.
beats.visual: Night sky from a01, now with the chain beneath

beats.say: A skill that was learned once can be learned again. That is the hope in every green cracker and every safer shed.
beats.caption: Learn again
beats.visual: Green cracker and new shed drawn side by side

beats.say: And its next lesson is how to keep the people who light it safe.
beats.visual: One lit match, held; fade to black (loops to the matchbox of a04)
